note: The six reader profiles of the Trade Explorer (contract 1.4: spec.context.persona). One source of truth: the page reads a copy (app/frontend/src/view/personas/, tests/test_personas.py checks it), the agent reads this file. A profile changes panels, wording, depth and questions, never a figure. Proto-personas grounded on the ONS persona research and the Eurostat user survey, not yet validated with STATEC users; model/personas_user_model.py holds the same readers as BESSER user models.

profiles.label: STATEC analyst
profiles.tagline: Every figure, its code, its query and its caveats
jury_link: Head of Economic conditions, modelling, forecasting

vocabulary.revealed comparative advantage: revealed comparative advantage (RCA, Balassa, against the 26 other EU countries)

suggested_questions: Why did exports jump in 2025?
Which CN8 lines explain the 2025 export change?
When did monthly exports shift for good since 1999?
Which forecasting method works best here?
profiles.prompt_snippet: The reader is a STATEC trade statistician. Give the full chain: the total, the HS2 chapter, the CN8 code and name, the partners, and what share of the change it explains. Write codes next to names (CN8 85171300). Name the method (STL, change-point penalty, ensemble with its backtest skill against the seasonal naive). Say which months of 2026 are provisional and that dates lining up are not causes. Draw the waterfall and the drill-down when a change is asked about. Up to six sentences.
leaves_when: a figure cannot be traced to a query
an AI rounds or computes a number
'not loaded' shows as zero
revisions and provisional months are not flagged

profiles.label: Policy adviser
profiles.tagline: Exposure, peers and outlook, ready for a briefing note
jury_link: Minister for the Economy (Journee de la Statistique)

vocabulary.RCA: specialisation (a product's share of Luxembourg's exports compared with the EU average)

suggested_questions: Show our exports to the United States. Show the months since 2023
How dependent is Luxembourg on its three neighbours?
Compare Luxembourg with Belgium and Germany
What should we expect for 2026?
profiles.prompt_snippet: The reader is a policy adviser preparing a note for a minister. Start with what it means (exposure, dependence, direction), then at most three figures. Compare with Belgium, Germany or the EU when it helps. Give a forecast as a range with its scenarios, in one sentence. No codes, no method names; one line of caveat. Four sentences at most, formal tone, neutral: describe, never recommend a policy.
leaves_when: jargon (RCA, CN8, MASE) without a plain meaning
no neutral source line to cite
an answer that takes a policy side
nothing to copy into a note

profiles.label: Journalist
profiles.tagline: The story, one chart and a sentence you can quote

vocabulary.RCA: goods Luxembourg sells more of than other EU countries

suggested_questions: Why did exports jump in 2025?
Where do the goods go?
What did COVID-19 do to trade?
Compare 2025 with 2024
profiles.prompt_snippet: The reader is a journalist on deadline. Lead with the one figure that is the story and the one reason the data shows for it. Name products in plain words (smartphones), never codes. Draw one chart at most, the one that tells the story (a route on the map or the crossroads). End with one sentence she can quote as is, then 'Source: Eurostat ds-045409, data produced by STATEC'. Three sentences at most. Say plainly what the data cannot show (causes).
leaves_when: the story is buried under method
the answer takes more than a few seconds
codes instead of names
no clear source line to credit

profiles.label: Business owner
profiles.tagline: Who buys your product line, and which markets grow

panel_titles.specialisation: Where Luxembourg sells more than its EU peers

vocabulary.RCA: specialisation (how much more of this product Luxembourg sells than the EU average)

suggested_questions: What has happened to our exports of steel H-sections to the United States since the new tariffs?
Who buys Luxembourg's rubber products?
Which markets grew most for plastics between 2024 and 2025?
Where is Luxembourg specialised and growing?
profiles.prompt_snippet: The reader exports goods from Luxembourg and looks for markets. Answer for the product group on the page (context product) unless he names another: who buys it, how much, which markets grew or are new. Show HS codes next to names, he uses them. Prefer a map or a two-year comparison by market. Four sentences at most. Never suggest a commercial decision; describe the data.
leaves_when: he cannot find his product code
only totals, no product detail
data that looks older than last year

profiles.label: Researcher
profiles.tagline: Methods, comparisons and the API call behind each chart
suggested_questions: Where is Luxembourg specialised and growing?
Is there a seasonal pattern in exports, by chapter?
Which forecasting method works best here?
How have the partners' ranks changed since 1999?
profiles.prompt_snippet: The reader is an economics researcher who will reproduce the result. Name the method and its parameters (STL period, change-point penalty and minimum size, forecast ensemble and backtest MASE), the dataset (Eurostat ds-045409) and the endpoint each figure came from. Mention limits: BLEU before 1999, provisional 2026 months, nominal euros, EU27 peers. Up to six sentences.
leaves_when: no API call or download behind a chart
a black-box answer with no method
figures that cannot be reproduced

profiles.label: Curious citizen
profiles.tagline: What Luxembourg buys and sells, in plain words

panel_titles.trend: Luxembourg buys more than it sells, every year since 1999

vocabulary.trade balance: the gap between what Luxembourg buys and sells
vocabulary.RCA: goods Luxembourg sells more of than other EU countries
vocabulary.forecast interval: a likely range, not a promise

suggested_questions: What does Luxembourg sell?
Who are Luxembourg's biggest customers?
Do we buy more than we sell?
What did COVID-19 do to trade?
profiles.prompt_snippet: The reader is a curious citizen, not a specialist, often on a phone. Use everyday words: goods bought abroad, goods sold abroad, kinds of goods; no codes, no abbreviations, no method names. One chart that answers the question, then at most three short sentences about it. Neutral and factual, no opinion on whether a figure is good or bad. If you give a forecast, say it is a likely range, not a promise.
leaves_when: jargon (HS, CN8, RCA, Herfindahl)
too many charts at once
text too small on a phone
a hint of bias or an agenda
